about: Plugin SELECTs whose plans may break the query-plan rule, each with the reason its plan is accepted. Copy an entry's id and statement from the report of `composer test:query-plans`. That run fails on an entry whose query it no longer sends, or whose query keeps the rule. An entry with `servers` (`mysql`, `mariadb`) holds only on those servers: it is judged, and judged stale, only on a run of one of them.

entries.statement: SELECT i.variant_id, i.location_id, i.held, COALESCE( SUM( h.quantity ), ? ) AS rows_sum FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items i LEFT JOIN {prefix}seocart_stock_holds h ON h.variant_id = i.variant_id AND h.location_id = i.location_id GROUP BY i.variant_id, i.location_id, i.held HAVING i.held <> rows_sum ORDER BY i.variant_id, i.location_id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's stock check compares every item's held, at every location, with the sum of its hold rows, so it reads every stock item by design; each item's holds are read by the item_expires index. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT i.variant_id, i.location_id, i.on_hand, COALESCE( SUM( l.delta ), ? ) AS ledger_sum, ( SELECT n.on_hand_after FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_ledger n WHERE n.variant_id = i.variant_id AND n.location_id = i.location_id ORDER BY n.id DESC LIMIT ? ) AS newest FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items i LEFT JOIN {prefix}seocart_stock_ledger l ON l.variant_id = i.variant_id AND l.location_id = i.location_id GROUP BY i.variant_id, i.location_id, i.on_hand HAVING ledger_sum <> i.on_hand OR ( newest IS NOT NULL AND newest <> i.on_hand ) ORDER BY i.variant_id, i.location_id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's stock check compares every item's on_hand, at every location, with the sum of its ledger there and with its newest entry there, so it reads every stock item by design; each item's ledger rows are read by the item_created index. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT i.variant_id, i.location_id, i.allocated, COALESCE( SUM( a.quantity - a.posted_quantity ), ? ) AS open_sum FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items i LEFT JOIN {prefix}seocart_stock_allocations a ON a.variant_id = i.variant_id AND a.location_id = i.location_id AND a.state = ? GROUP BY i.variant_id, i.location_id, i.allocated HAVING i.allocated <> open_sum ORDER BY i.variant_id, i.location_id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's stock check compares every item's allocated, at every location, with its open allocations there, so it reads every stock item by design; each item's allocations are read by the item_state index. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT h.variant_id, h.location_id, h.hold_group, SUM( h.quantity ) AS quantity FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_holds h LEFT JOIN {prefix}seocart_stock_items i ON i.variant_id = h.variant_id AND i.location_id = h.location_id WHERE i.variant_id IS NULL GROUP BY h.variant_id, h.location_id, h.hold_group ORDER BY h.variant_id, h.location_id, h.hold_group LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's stock check looks for hold rows whose stock item is gone, which no reclaim can give back, so it reads every hold row by design; each row's item is found by its primary key. The table holds only live checkout holds and expired ones the sweep has yet to reclaim. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT p.id FROM {prefix}seocart_products p LEFT JOIN {prefix}seocart_variants v ON v.product_id = p.id AND v.combination_hash = ? LEFT JOIN {prefix}seocart_variant_prices vp ON vp.variant_id = v.id AND vp.currency = ? WHERE p.generation_state = ? AND ( p.enabled_variant_count = ? OR v.id IS NULL OR vp.id IS NULL ) ORDER BY p.id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's check for a complete product that is not actually whole starts from every complete product, found by the generation_state index, looking for zero enabled variants or a missing base-currency price; about half of a real catalog is complete, so the index legitimately hands back thousands of candidate rows before the LEFT JOINs narrow them. The default variant and its price are each then found by their own unique key. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT post_id, product_id, locale FROM {prefix}seocart_product_posts WHERE post_id > ? ORDER BY post_id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's translation-group check must ask the multilingual plugin about every bound post to find the ones its binding disagrees with, so it walks the whole product_posts table by its primary key, a page at a time; a cursor part-way through legitimately leaves thousands of rows ahead of it. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT id, scope, TIMESTAMPDIFF( SECOND, created_at, UTC_TIMESTAMP() ) AS age_seconds FROM {prefix}seocart_idempotency_keys WHERE state = ? AND created_at <= UTC_TIMESTAMP() - INTERVAL ? SECOND ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's check for idempotency keys stranded in `claimed` reads the whole key table, oldest first: a stranded key is rare, and the table holds only the keys of the retention period, which the retention job keeps to that. An index on (state, created_at) would be written by every claim and every completion of an order placement for doctor alone. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT DISTINCT variant_id, location_id FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_holds WHERE expires_at <= UTC_TIMESTAMP() AND reclaim_token IS NULL AND ( variant_id > ? OR ( variant_id = ? AND location_id > ? ) ) ORDER BY variant_id, location_id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: MariaDB only. The hold sweep's page of items with expired holds walks the item_expires index from its cursor, an item at a location, and stops at its LIMIT. MariaDB estimates the whole range past the cursor without the LIMIT (11952 of 11949 rows on the medium dataset); MySQL plans the same walk at 240 rows and keeps the rule.

entries.statement: SELECT v.id FROM {prefix}seocart_variants v JOIN {prefix}seocart_products p ON p.id = v.product_id AND v.id > ? ORDER BY v.id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: MariaDB only. Doctor's missing-stock-item check pages the variant ids by the primary key from its cursor, each product joined by its own primary key, and stops at its LIMIT. MariaDB estimates the whole range past the cursor without the LIMIT (9944 of 10000 rows on the medium dataset); MySQL keeps the rule (4937 rows).

entries.statement: SELECT location_id, SUM( on_hand ) AS on_hand FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items WHERE location_id IN ( ?+ ) GROUP BY location_id ORDER BY location_id
entries.reason: The list of locations shows each location's units on hand, so it adds up every stock item of the locations it lists by design: one range of the location_on_hand index, which holds both columns it reads, grouped by location (5499 of 10333 rows estimated on the medium dataset, nearly all at the default location). It is a merchant's list, read by the locations screen and `wp seocart location list`, never on a request a shopper makes.

entries.statement: SELECT t.id, ( SELECT COALESCE( SUM( l.quantity - l.received_quantity - l.lost_quantity ), ? ) FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfer_lines l WHERE l.transfer_id = t.id ) AS on_the_way, ( SELECT COALESCE( SUM( m.lost_quantity ), ? ) FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfer_lines m WHERE m.transfer_id = t.id ) AS lost, COALESCE( g.total, ? ) AS moved FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfers t LEFT JOIN ( SELECT transfer_id, SUM( - delta ) AS total FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_ledger WHERE transfer_id IS NOT NULL AND reason IN ( ?+ ) GROUP BY transfer_id ) g ON g.transfer_id = t.id WHERE t.state IN ( ?+ ) HAVING on_the_way <> moved - lost ORDER BY t.id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's transit check compares every sent transfer's units on the way, by its lines, with what its ledger entries moved less what was lost, so it reads every transfer in transit or received by design: MySQL by the state_created index (7206 of 12000 rows estimated on the plan run, most of whose transfers are received), MariaDB by the primary key (12012). Each transfer's lines are read by the transfer_id index, and the ledger entries that name a transfer are totalled once, by the ledger's transfer_id index. It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT t.id, t.order_id FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfers t WHERE t.state = ? AND t.kind = ? AND EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfer_lines l WHERE l.transfer_id = t.id AND l.lost_quantity > ? AND l.allocation_id IS NOT NULL ) ORDER BY t.id DESC LIMIT ?
entries.reason: Doctor's shortage check looks through the received transfers an order waited for, newest first, for a line that lost the order's units, so it reads them by design: MySQL starts from the received transfers, by the state_created index (6006 of 12000 rows estimated on the plan run, most of whose transfers are received), and reads each one's lines by the transfer_id index; MariaDB walks the transfers by the primary key, newest first, and reads the lines that carry an allocation by the allocation_id index (11894 of 12000 rows estimated). It runs from `wp seocart doctor`, never on a request a shopper or a merchant makes.

entries.statement: SELECT variant_id FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items WHERE location_id = ? AND variant_id > ? AND on_hand - allocated - held > ? ORDER BY variant_id LIMIT ?
entries.reason: A deactivation's move of a location's available stock finds, a page at a time from its cursor, the location's items with units to move, so each page reads the location's items by design: MySQL by the location_on_hand index (5166 of 10333 rows estimated on the medium dataset), MariaDB by the primary key from the cursor (10333). It runs in the move's background job after a merchant deactivates a location that holds stock, never on a request a shopper makes.

entries.statement: SELECT EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_ledger WHERE location_id = ? ) AS ledger, EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items WHERE location_id = ? AND ( on_hand <> ? OR allocated <> ? OR held <> ? ) ) AS stock, EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_items i JOIN {prefix}seocart_stock_holds h ON h.variant_id = i.variant_id AND h.location_id = i.location_id WHERE i.location_id = ? ) AS holds, EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_allocations WHERE location_id = ? ) AS allocations, EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfers WHERE source_location_id = ? ) AS transfers_out, EXISTS ( SELECT ? FROM {prefix}seocart_stock_transfers WHERE destination_location_id = ? ) AS transfers_in
entries.reason: Before a location is deleted, this check asks whether anything still names it, and each EXISTS stops at the first index entry for the location. The two over transfers are read by the source_state and destination_state indexes, whose estimate counts every transfer from or to the location (on the plan run, whose transfers are all between its two locations, 6006 of 12000 rows on MySQL and up to 10004 on MariaDB), not the one entry read. It runs when a merchant deletes a location, never on a request a shopper makes.
